<div class="card card-retractable" style="margin-bottom: 2rem;" onclick="this.classList.toggle('expanded')">

  <p style="text-align: center;font-weight: bold; font-size: 28px;">
  Challenges
  </p>
  I had an **extremely limited time** (10 minutes) to communicate a **complex concept** to a **diverse audience** (from biologists to data scientists) not specialised in TPP.
  I needed to:

  - explain the core idea clearly, without going in the details while not sounding vague;
  - **generate interest** in a niche methodological topic;
  - convey both **technical value and broader impact**;
  - **inspire** people to think about accessibility to sciences.
</div>

<div class="card-row">
  
  <div class="card card-retractable" onclick="this.classList.toggle('expanded')">
  <p style="text-align: center;font-weight: bold; font-size: 28px;">
  Approach
  </p>
  I structured the talk around **impact-driven storytelling**, rather than technical depth. 
  <br><br>
  Key elements:

  - using clear, structured slides to guide a **fast-paced, engaging narrative**;
  - focusing on the core concept (the need for higher throughtput for more reliable data analysis) and its practical implications, rather than full technical detail
  **highlighting benefits at two levels**:

    - **practical**: improving results while reducing experimental effort;
    - **systemic**: enabling broader access to advanced methods across labs.

  <!--Output: Slide deck designed for clarity, pacing, and impact-->
  </div>

  <div class="card card-retractable" onclick="this.classList.toggle('expanded')">
  <p style="text-align: center;font-weight: bold; font-size: 28px;">
  Strengths
  </p>
  - Ability to **communicate complex ideas** concisely under **strong time constraints**;
  - **persuasive storytelling** for scientific and technical audiences;
  - framing technical work in terms of **real-world and societal impact**;
  - engaging diverse audiences with **different backgrounds**;
  - **bridging the needs** of experimentalists with the capabilities of data scientists;
  - making a **long-lasting impression, inspiring** scientists to considere this issue and what they could do on their side to improve it.
  </div>
</div>

<div class="card card-retractable" style="margin-bottom: 2rem;" onclick="this.classList.toggle('expanded')">
<p style="text-align: center;font-weight: bold; font-size: 28px;">
Impact
</p>
In the current academical research world, it is all about having enough money to pursuie research. However, like everywhere else, **wealth is distributed in an unfair manner, and poorer labs are stuck** in a vivious circle: to get grants, researchers needs publications in highly ranked  journals, for which articles' submission is extremely expensive. Those journals also expect exceptional results, often achievable with state-of-the-art scientific assays, which are, them too, particularly costly. Thus, the richest groups manage to publish more regularly in the best journals, being able to afford the price of publications and experimentation, and in turn, to get the next grants. 
<br> <br>
I believe that **brilliant and revolutionnary ideas are not restricted to scientists who made it to the richests labs**. Thus, lowering the wealth barrier would give a chance to **Science to integrate more diverse ideas and researchs, to move faster and further**.

</div>
